hero.title: Understanding Lua
hero.description: A short, practical introduction to Lua — the language most FiveM scripts are written in. Below you can also write your own code and have it checked instantly.

sections.title: How Lua scripts work
sections.lead: Six building blocks that show up in almost every FiveM script.

items.title: Variables
items.description: `local` stores values your script remembers — names, numbers, or true/false flags.

items.title: Conditionals
items.description: `if / then / else / end` lets your script react differently depending on the situation.

items.title: Loops
items.description: `for ... do ... end` or `ipairs()` let you go through lists without writing out every entry by hand.

items.title: Tables
items.description: A table (`{}`) is Lua's central data structure — it can store lists and named fields at the same time.

items.title: Functions
items.description: A function bundles reusable logic under a name you can call anywhere in the script.

items.title: FiveM Events
items.description: `RegisterCommand` and `TriggerClientEvent` are how server and client scripts talk to each other.

playground.title: Try it yourself
playground.lead: Write the matching code in the field and click "Check" — you'll get instant feedback.

challenges.title: Declare a variable
challenges.instructions: Declare a local variable named `level` with the value `5`.
challenges.hint: Use the `local` keyword, followed by the name, an `=`, and the value: local level = 5

challenges.title: Write an if statement
challenges.instructions: The variable `cash` is already given. Write an `if` statement that checks whether `cash` is greater than or equal to 100.

challenges.title: Write a for loop
challenges.instructions: The table `players` is already given. Write a `for` loop using `ipairs` that goes through every entry.
challenges.hint: Structure: for index, name in ipairs(players) do ... end

challenges.title: Create a table
challenges.instructions: Create a local table named `player` with the field `cash = 500`.

challenges.title: Define a function
challenges.instructions: Write a local function named `heal` that takes one parameter.

frameworksTeaser.title: ESX, QBCore or Qbox?
frameworksTeaser.lead: A short overview of how the three major FiveM frameworks work and differ.

hero.title: ESX, QBCore & Qbox
hero.description: A framework gives a FiveM server its core systems — jobs, inventory, banking and more — so every script doesn't start from zero. I develop for all three major frameworks equally.

intro.title: What a framework handles
intro.lead: Nearly every framework ships these core systems — scripts build on top of them instead of reinventing them.

cards.title: The three big options
cards.lead: Each framework has a different maturity level and target audience.

items.name: ESX
items.description: The historical market leader with the largest script catalog around and very beginner-friendly. New feature development has, however, largely stalled.
items.bestFor: Best for: existing ESX servers that don't need a full rebuild.

items.name: QBCore
items.description: The modern standard since 2020, with cleaner code and better performance than ESX, plus a huge ecosystem of free and premium scripts. Active development has also largely stalled here.
items.bestFor: Best for: servers built on the large existing QBCore script ecosystem.

items.name: Qbox
items.description: A community fork of QBCore that pushes modularity and modern Lua practices further (including ox_lib), while staying largely backwards compatible with existing QBCore resources.
items.bestFor: Best for: new servers in 2026 that want an actively maintained foundation.

rows.name: QBCore
rows.ecosystem: Very large, lots of premium content

frameworks.positioning: Whether your server already runs on ESX or QBCore, or you want to start fresh with Qbox in 2026 — I build scripts and customizations for all three frameworks.
